archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-reliant)
archetype.definition: A dual-threat quarterback whose legs now show up mostly when plays break down rather than on called runs, paired with a downfield arm that still produces while the quick, short game has stalled.

report.headline: Downfield passing still works; the short game and protection are failing him.
report.take:
Hurts has been one of the league's most reliable efficiency quarterbacks for four straight years. From 2022 through 2025 his EPA per play never ranked worse than 22nd, and his CPOE sat between +2.7 and +7.5. Five games into 2026 he is at -0.058 EPA per dropback (31st of 43) with a -2.55 CPOE, and the Eagles are 2-3. That is a real break from his track record, so the question is what caused it.

The depth splits answer most of it. On 46 throws of 10+ air yards he has been excellent: +0.92 EPA on intermediate throws with a +7.9 CPOE, and +0.80 on deep shots with a +10.1 CPOE. Six of his eight touchdowns came there. Everything near the line is broken. Twenty-two throws behind the line of scrimmage produced -0.89 EPA with a 9% success rate. Eighty-six short throws came in at -0.22 with a -6.2 CPOE, and the under-center game is completing 37.5%. When the easy completions fail, he lives on third-and-long (8.8 yards to go on average), and the offense ranks dead last in success rate. That points to the structure around him: the screen and checkdown game, a line that lost Lane Johnson to retirement and is missing center Drew Kendall, and a backfield thinned by Saquon Barkley's hamstring. His arm talent looks intact.

The numbers flatter one thing and hide another. The sacks look like a pocket problem: 7.8% sack rate and 36.4% pressure-to-sack, 31st of 36. But he has always been a hold-it-and-extend quarterback. His pressure-to-sack hit 38.4% in 2022 and 41.8% in 2024, both strong seasons. What is new is the bad-throw rate, 15.6% against a career norm around 13-14%, and that is concentrated in a 36% bad-throw game against the Rams. On the other side, the rushing value is fading. Designed runs are averaging 1.1 yards with a 55.6% stuff rate, his carries fell to two in London, and his season rushing totals have trended down since 2021. The scrambles, at +0.33 EPA, are now the only part of the run game paying off.

Week 5 may be the template from here. Against the league's third-best defense he got the ball out in 2.53 seconds, took one sack and threw 220 yards in a near-upset. If Philadelphia keeps him in rhythm and DeVonta Smith and Barkley return, his efficiency should drift back toward neutral or better. The downfield profile is too good and too consistent with his career to stay attached to a bottom-third EPA.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep accuracy intact
strengths.body: Beyond 10 air yards he is completing throws well above expectation and generating big EPA. Six of his eight touchdowns came on these throws. It matches a career-long downfield profile, so it is the most bankable part of his game even if the 46-throw sample inflates the exact rates.

strengths.title: Scrambles still create value
strengths.body: His 12 scrambles averaged +0.33 EPA and produced five first downs. That makes them the one part of his rushing that works, and it partly pays for his long time to throw. It is a skill he has carried for years, so it should hold.

strengths.title: Red-zone finishing
strengths.body: Five touchdowns and one interception on 14 red-zone throws, with a +14.8 CPOE, kept the scoring respectable while the offense struggled between the 20s. The sample is tiny, so expect the rate to cool. His size and goal-line legs keep the floor reasonable.

concerns.title: Short and behind-the-line game collapsed
concerns.body: Over 100 throws near the line have produced negative EPA, with a 9% success rate on throws behind the line. That keeps the offense behind the chains and drives its 32nd-ranked success rate. Much of this traces to screens, backs and timing being out of sync with a reshuffled line and a missing Barkley. It should improve as health returns, but it is the biggest drag right now.

concerns.title: Sacks and protection without Johnson
concerns.body: His pressure-to-sack rate is 31st, and he is being hit or sacked on 16.8% of dropbacks. Long holds are his long-standing trade-off; he posted similar rates in good years. The added problem is losing a 100%-snap right tackle to retirement and his center to injury. That is structural and won't fully fix itself this season.

concerns.title: Designed-run game drying up
concerns.body: Called runs are averaging 1.1 yards and getting stuffed more than half the time. His weekly rushing fell to 2 yards in Week 5. His season rushing totals have declined over several years, so some of this is who he is becoming, not just a bad sample.

trend.note: He opened with two positive passing games against bottom-10 defenses. Then came -11 and -8.2 passing EPA against Chicago and the Rams. The quick-game approach in London (-0.6 EPA against the third-ranked defense) looked like a floor stabilizing rather than a turnaround.

nextGame.headline: A low-pressure Carolina defense suits a quarterback losing to sacks
nextGame.body:
Carolina's defense ranks 21st in EPA and 20th against the pass. Most importantly, it is 31st in QB hit rate and 25th in sack rate, which strips away the main thing sinking Hurts. The Panthers limit explosive passes (4th), but when deep balls connect they get burned (27th in deep EPA). That fits a passer whose best work this year has come downfield. Quarterbacks have averaged 279 passing yards a game against them (27th), and tight ends have beaten their norms by 4.1 PPR points (27th). Lead receivers have been held well under their averages, though, so the volume may flow through Dallas Goedert and the secondary options rather than the WR1.

Availability is the swing. Barkley and DeVonta Smith are listed out with hamstrings, but Sirianni is hopeful both play. Will Shipley is doubtful with a partial plantar fascia tear, so the backfield may be thin if Barkley sits. Kendall remains out and Johnson is gone, so the protection issues travel. On Carolina's side, the absences mostly hit its offensive line: Ekwonu and Moton are out, and Freeling and Lewis are questionable. That matters less for Hurts than for the overall script, since the Panthers' sixth-ranked passing offense is facing a Philadelphia defense that ranks 24th against the pass.

keyMatchups.title: Hurts' clock versus a weak rush
keyMatchups.body: Carolina rarely hits quarterbacks, which should let his 3-second operation work without drive-killing sacks. If the line holds up for even average time, his intermediate game should get room.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots against a leaky back end
keyMatchups.body: The Panthers allow few explosives but pay heavily when one lands. Hurts has a +10.1 CPOE on deep throws. One or two connections could swing his line.

keyMatchups.title: Goedert and Wicks over the WR1
keyMatchups.body: Carolina has held lead receivers 6 PPR points under their averages but let tight ends run 4.1 over. Goedert (+0.45 EPA per target) and Wicks (+0.74) have been his most efficient reads, and the matchup steers volume toward them.

nextGame.watch: Whether Philadelphia keeps the quick-game structure from London and how many sacks he takes. A one- or two-sack game against this pass rush would signal the passing offense is back on track.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect improvement toward the passer he has been, though not all the way back. The downfield accuracy, scramble value and red-zone size have years behind them. The short-game collapse and -2.55 CPOE are well outside his career range and should normalize as Smith and Barkley get healthy and the line settles. The pieces likely to regress are the red-zone touchdown efficiency and the huge EPA on 17 deep attempts. The structural pieces likely to stick are the protection without Johnson and a designed-run game that has been shrinking for years.

A realistic landing spot is a roughly neutral-to-slightly-positive EPA quarterback for the remaining games. Passing volume should creep up from his current 187 yards a game, and rushing production will sit below his old 600-plus-yard pace, carried mostly by scrambles and goal-line work.
swingFactors: Health of Barkley and DeVonta Smith
Interior and right-tackle protection without Johnson and Kendall
Whether the quick game from Week 5 sticks

bets.reason: Carolina allows 279 passing yards a game to quarterbacks (27th) and ranks 31st in QB hit rate. That removes the sacks that have been killing his drives. Carolina's sixth-ranked passing offense should also keep Philadelphia throwing.

Designed runs are averaging 1.1 yards with a 55.6% stuff rate. His weekly rushing has gone 46, 16, 25, 18, 2. His legs now show up mainly on scrambles, which a low-pressure defense will force less often.

Philadelphia is 0-3 against the spread as a favorite this year, with an offense 29th in EPA and dead last in success rate. Carolina's offense ranks 8th and its pass attack 6th, facing an Eagles pass defense that is 24th with the league's worst hit rate.

confidence.note: Five-game sample, depth splits on small attempts, and key teammates' availability for Sunday still uncertain.
